item.title: Ukraine refutes Slovakia's claim it cut emergency electricity supplies
item.description: However, Ukraine's state grid operator, Ukrenergo, said it received a notice from Slovakia's energy regulator about new flexible price conditions for emergency imports, Vitaliy Zaichenko, Ukrenergo's CEO, told the Kyiv Independent.

item.title: Explosion hits Dnipro police building in second attack on law enforcement in 24 hours
item.description: While no casualties were reported in the Dnipro incident, the blast caused significant damage to the building's interior, office equipment, and a nearby vehicle.

item.title: Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant left with just 22 reactor operators, far below safety levels
item.description: The plant, legally owned by Energoatom, once employed 159 licensed specialists — the only people authorized to directly operate the plant’s six nuclear reactors, which, prewar, provided over a fifth of Ukraine’s electricity.

item.title: 'No coincidence' — Mykolaiv explosion that injured 7 police officers treated as terrorism following fatal Lviv attack
item.description: "The enemy is deliberately trying to kill Ukrainian police officers who stand guard every day to protect the people and the state," the chief of Ukraine's National Police, Ivan Vyhivsky, said.

item.title: EU fails to send Russia 'powerful signal' as Hungary blocks 20th sanctions package
item.description: "This is a setback and a message we didn't want to send today," EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said.

item.title: Moscow police vehicle targeted in blast near major railway station, 1 officer killed
item.description: An explosion at Moscow's Savyolovsky railway station square killed one traffic police officer and wounded two others late on Feb. 23, according to Russia’s Interior Ministry and Investigative Committee.

item.title: Explosion during ammunition demonstration injures two students at Dnipro school
item.description: An explosion occurred at a Ukrainian school in the city of Dnipro on Feb. 23 during a classroom demonstration of ammunition, injuring two children, according to regional police.

item.title: Zelensky warns Belarus can no longer deny involvement as Russian drone repeaters operate there, says future peaceful relations depend on free leadership and pro-EU path in Minsk
item.description: President Volodymyr Zelensky said in an interview with Belarusian independent outlet Dzerkalo that Russia has deployed Shahed drone repeaters in Belarus to help coordinate attacks on Ukraine, warning that Minsk can no longer deny responsibility while also expressing hope for future EU integration between the two countries under democratic leadership.
